results.name: Celebratory Hip Thrust
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight up in the air.
Simultaneously bend your elbows and thrust your arms downwards to your hips while thrusting your hips forward.
Return to the initial position with your arms extended overhead and your hips back in the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with a controlled pace, focusing on the coordinated motion of your arms and hips.
Use the downward thrust of your arms to help generate momentum for the hip thrust.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor to maintain stability.
results.description: Celebratory Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Chest Fly Side Step
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees, and your elbows open wide at shoulder height.
Step your right foot out to the side, bending your right knee slightly as you bring your elbows together in front of you until they are close together and back.
Return to the starting position by stepping your left foot out to the side while repeating the fly motion with your arms.
Repeat the movement alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your arms remain bent at the elbows throughout the chest fly motion.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your elbows together in front of you.
results.description: Chest Fly Side Step is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Chest Pull Back
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and leaning slightly forward at the hips. Bend your arms in front of your chest with your palms facing each other, lightly squeezing to activate your chest.
Perform a rowing motion with your right arm by pulling it back, bending your elbow, and squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Return your right arm to the starting position, keeping your left arm steady and engaged in front of your chest.
Repeat the rowing motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine to maximize the engagement of you back muscles.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to ensure proper muscle activation.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Ensure your chest remains open and engaged by maintaining light tension between your palms.
results.description: Chest Pull Back is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Chest Raise and Rotate
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees, with forearms parallel to the floor, elbows squeezed to the sides.
Perform a semi-circular motion by rotating your arms upwards and outwards until your forearms are vertical to the floor and your upper arms are at shoulder level.
Reverse the motion, bringing your arms back to the starting position with your forearms parallel to the floor.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on maintaining a 90-degree bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to ensure proper form.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling as you lift your arms and exhaling as you lower them.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to support your lower back and enhance balance.
results.description: Chest Raise and Rotate is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Circle Elbow Arm
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder level, keeping them straight.
Bend your arms at the elbows, bringing your fingers to touch your shoulders on the same side, keeping your elbows pointing outwards.
Begin to make small circular motions with your elbows, moving them forward, up, back, and down in a controlled manner.
Continue circling your elbows for the desired number of repetitions, then reverse the direction of the circles and repeat.
tips: Focus on making smooth and controlled movements to maximize muscle activation and avoid straining your joints.
Perform the movement slowly to maintain control and improve shoulder mobility.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, maintaining a consistent rhythm.
results.description: Circle Elbow Arm is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Chest.

results.name: Clap Jack
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet together and your arms extended by your sides at shoulder level.
Simultaneously jump your feet out to the sides to a wide stance while bringing your arms straight in front of you and clapping your hands together at chest level.
Jump your feet back together and bring your arms back to your sides to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement continuously for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Ensure your knees are slightly bent during the jumps to absorb impact and protect your joints.
Breathe rhythmically throughout the exercise, exhaling as you jump out and clap, and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on maintaining a consistent rhythm and avoiding excessive arm or leg movements to maximize efficiency.
results.description: Clap Jack is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Control Balance
instructions: Lie down on your back, raise your legs towards the head, and hold your feet by extending your arms overhead.
Release your right leg and take it upward until it becomes vertical to the floor.
Place your free hand on your left calf and maintain balance.
Hold for a while, return to the starting position, and repeat.
tips: Perform the movement with control, especially when lifting and lowering your legs, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain on the floor and avoid straining your neck.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your leg and inhaling as you lower it.
Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort during the exercise.
results.description: Control Balance is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Hamstrings.

results.name: Corner Touch
instructions: Begin standing with your body turned to the left side in a semi-lunge position, your left leg bent, and your right leg extended behind you lightly bent. Extend your right arm upward and your left arm downward to your side.

Engage your core and rotate your body on your feet, turning to face the opposite side. As you rotate, lower your right arm and raise your left arm, so that your left arm is now upward and your right arm is downward to your side.
Repeat the movement, alternating sides, and performing the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using a controlled motion when rotating your body to avoid straining your back.
Ensure you stay in place as you rotate, using a controlled motion to maintain balance and stability.
Ensure your movements are smooth and deliberate to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you rotate and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Corner Touch is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back.

results.name: Crawl With Sled Drag
instructions: Attach a light sled to a harness or belt around your waist.
Get on your hands and feet in a bear-crawl position with your knees just off the floor.
Crawl forward, moving opposite hand and foot together, dragging the sled behind you.
Continue for the set distance with your back flat.
tips: Keep your hips level and low.
Take small, controlled steps.
results.description: Crawl With Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes, Triceps.

results.name: Criss Cross Arms Lift
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight in front of you at your hip height, palms facing inwards.
Cross your right arm over your left arm at the wrists and then cross your left arm over your right arm.
Repeat the crossing movement until your hands are opposite your head.
Lower your arms back to your hip level by crossing them down.
tips: Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift and lower your arms, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
results.description: Criss Cross Arms Lift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.
